note: Every tunable constant the build enforces, in one file. SPEC.md Appendix B lists the completeness weights and the prose-similarity threshold as open items to tune against the pilot batch (Phase 8); they live here so tuning them is a one-line change with no code to edit.

publicationFloor.note: SPEC.md §5.9 — below this an entry gets no page of its own. It still exists as a catalogue row and in cartridge and maker listings. Enforced where pages are generated (Phase 4), NOT by the content gate: a thin entry is incomplete, not broken, and failing the build on it would push authors toward padding.

familyPublicationFloor.note: SPEC.md §5.9's floor is model-shaped: it asks for six verified core specs, and a `kind: 'family'` entry has no mass, no length and no barrel because a platform spans manufacturers (SPEC.md §5.1). Applying the model floor to a family made the AR-15 an unlinked catalogue row while its page existed and was linked from its own members. A family's substance is its computed member list and its prose, and `family/no-members` already fails the build when that list is empty, so what is left to require here is an image and real prose.

completeness.note: SPEC.md §5.9 — tier is COMPUTED from this score, never asserted by an author. Only `verified` values count: an estimated figure contributes nothing, so estimating your way to a full page produces a Tier 3 entry covered in amber badges. Inventing numbers buys nothing. Weights are provisional until the pilot batch.

tierFloor.note: Score at or above which an entry reaches each tier. Tier 3 is the floor and has no minimum.

prose.note: SPEC.md §13 gate 4 — the near-duplicate prose gate. With many parallel authors writing about mechanically similar arms, boilerplate is a certainty rather than a risk. Shingled Jaccard similarity over windows of `shingleWords` words; at or above `maxSimilarity` the build fails naming BOTH files. Narratives yielding fewer than `minShingles` shingles are too short to compare and are skipped — thinness is the publication floor's job, not this gate's.

assets.note: SPEC.md §10. Per-file caps alone are not enough — a thousand compliant files still overrun a 1 GB Pages site — so `check:assets` also enforces a running total and prints usage on every build. Hero and gallery are told apart by filename: `hero.webp` is the hero, every other file is gallery.
